hook.text: One consumer handles 10K events per second. The producer just hit 100K. You need ten times the throughput.

buildup.text: Adding more consumers to a group distributes partitions across them, multiplying processing capacity.

discovery.text: The maximum parallelism equals the number of partitions. More consumers than partitions means idle workers.

twist.text: Rebalancing — redistributing partitions when consumers join or leave — causes brief processing pauses.

climax.text: Planning partition counts at topic creation time sets the ceiling for future consumer scalability.

punchline.text: Scale the consumers. But plan the partitions first.

quiz.question: What limits the maximum consumer parallelism in Kafka?
options: The number of partitions in the topic
The number of brokers in the cluster
